title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
authors: Shunyu Yao; Jeffrey Zhao; Dian Yu; Nan Du; Izhak Shafran; Karthik Narasimhan; Yuan Cao
research_question: Can interleaved reasoning and action improve tool-grounded problem solving?
dataset_or_environment: HotpotQA; FEVER; ALFWorld; WebShop
models_or_agents: Prompted LLM agents using ReAct
methodology: Interleave thought traces and environment actions; compare with reasoning-only and acting baselines
metrics: Task success; human interpretability
key_findings: Interleaving observations with reasoning improved task outcomes in the reported settings and lets agents revise action plans after observations.
limitations: It is a general architecture paper; it does not define a calibrated stop decision, conclusive negative evidence, or a cyber safety oracle.
relevance_to_project: Establishes the trace unit (action-observation loop), but does not answer when persistence should end.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Noah Shinn; Federico Cassano; Ashwin Gopinath; Karthik Narasimhan; Shunyu Yao
research_question: Can linguistic feedback and episodic reflection improve agents through trial and error without updating weights?
dataset_or_environment: Sequential decision-making tasks; coding; language reasoning; HumanEval
models_or_agents: Reflexion agent with reflective memory
methodology: Use scalar or textual feedback to generate a reflection that conditions later trials; include feedback/memory ablations
metrics: Task success; pass@1; ablation outcomes
key_findings: Reported improvements show that feedback can be converted into later-trial adaptation.
limitations: Most learning occurs across attempts and is optimized for eventual success; no principal measure separates a justified stop from needless continuation inside an episode.
relevance_to_project: A key baseline for recovery mechanisms; the new study must distinguish within-episode behavior from cross-trial reflection.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
authors: Aman Madaan; Niket Tandon; Prakhar Gupta; Skyler Hallinan; Luyu Gao; Sarah Wiegreffe; Uri Alon; Nouha Dziri; Shrimai Prabhumoye; Yiming Yang; Shashank Gupta; Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder; Katherine Hermann; Sean Welleck; Amir Yazdanbakhsh; Peter Clark
research_question: Can a single model iteratively improve its own output using self-generated feedback?
dataset_or_environment: Seven tasks including code rewriting, constrained generation, reasoning, and dialogue
models_or_agents: GPT-3.5; ChatGPT; GPT-4 as generator, feedback source, and refiner
methodology: Generate, critique, and refine repeatedly without external training
metrics: Human preference and task-specific automatic metrics
key_findings: The paper reports improvement over direct generation across its evaluated tasks.
limitations: Output refinement is not the same as an agent interpreting ground-truth external failure; it does not study action costs, stopping, or adversarial task feedback.
relevance_to_project: Useful contrast: extra iterations can help, so a stopping study must not equate every repeat with failure.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
authors: Xiao Liu; Hao Yu; Hanchen Zhang; Yifan Xu; Xuanyu Lei; Hanyu Lai; Yu Gu; Hangliang Ding; Kaiwen Men; Kejuan Yang; Shudan Zhang; Xiang Deng; Aohan Zeng; Zhengxiao Du; Chenhui Zhang; Sheng Shen; Tianjun Zhang; Yu Su; Huan Sun; Minlie Huang; Yuxiao Dong; Jie Tang
research_question: How capable are LLMs as agents across interactive environments?
dataset_or_environment: Eight environments spanning operating-system, database, knowledge-graph, web, card-game, household, lateral-thinking, and shopping tasks
models_or_agents: 29 API and open-weight LLMs with a common agent interface
methodology: Benchmark diverse environments and analyze reported finish reasons
metrics: Environment success and failure-category analyses
key_findings: It identifies long-term reasoning, decision-making, and instruction following as recurring failure sources.
limitations: Failure categories are not a prespecified causal taxonomy of post-negative-evidence behavior; most reporting remains endpoint-oriented.
relevance_to_project: Shows that generic agent evaluation already analyzes failures, narrowing any claim of novelty to a more specific trace/evidence design.

title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
authors: Chang Ma; Junlei Zhang; Zhihao Zhu; Cheng Yang; Yujiu Yang; Yaohui Jin; Zhenzhong Lan; Lingpeng Kong; Junxian He
research_question: Can intermediate progress make multi-turn agent evaluation more informative than final success alone?
dataset_or_environment: Nine task types and 1,013 partially observable environments
models_or_agents: Unified text agents; reported proprietary and open-weight LLMs
methodology: Human-authored subgoals and progress-rate tracking with trajectory inspection
metrics: Success; fine-grained progress rate; grounding; long-range interaction
key_findings: Progress metrics reveal differences hidden by near-zero final success rates.
limitations: Progress is not evidence calibration: it does not label whether a failed hypothesis was abandoned, revisited rationally, or pursued after conclusive evidence.
relevance_to_project: A direct precedent against framing the project as the first process-sensitive agent evaluation.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Carlos E. Jimenez; John Yang; Alexander Wettig; Shunyu Yao; Kexin Pei; Ofir Press; Karthik R. Narasimhan
research_question: Can language models resolve real repository issues from issue descriptions and test suites?
dataset_or_environment: 2,294 issue/PR pairs from 12 Python repositories
models_or_agents: Proprietary LMs and SWE-Llama
methodology: Provide codebase plus issue; score a submitted patch through tests
metrics: Resolved rate / test-based outcome
key_findings: It established a realistic repository-and-execution evaluation format, with low original solve rates.
limitations: It is general software repair, not security or failed-attack adaptation; issue text may contain solution information.
relevance_to_project: Provides the execution-and-replay pattern, but not a valid success/stop taxonomy.

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
authors: John Yang; Carlos E. Jimenez; Alexander Wettig; Kilian Lieret; Shunyu Yao; Karthik Narasimhan; Ofir Press
research_question: How does the computer interface shape coding-agent performance?
dataset_or_environment: SWE-bench and HumanEvalFix
models_or_agents: GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus in the SWE-agent scaffold
methodology: Design and ablate an agent-computer interface for search, editing, and feedback
metrics: pass@1 / resolve rate; ablations
key_findings: The interface and feedback format materially change observed agent behavior and outcomes.
limitations: A harness is a treatment, not neutral plumbing; its study does not specify stop rationality or security feedback.
relevance_to_project: Requires frozen tool/interface conditions and supports treating model-plus-harness as the experimental unit.

title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
authors: Shunyu Yao; Noah Shinn; Pedram Razavi; Karthik Narasimhan
research_question: Can tool-using agents follow rules and change an external database state reliably during dynamic user interaction?
dataset_or_environment: Retail and airline tool-user environments
models_or_agents: Function-calling agents including GPT-4o
methodology: Compare final database state with annotated goal state over repeated trials
metrics: Final-state success; pass^k reliability
key_findings: It uses state-based evaluation and finds substantial inconsistency across repeated agent trials.
limitations: It is not cyber-specific and does not distinguish deliberate stop, repeated hypothesis, or feedback strength.
relevance_to_project: Supports use of independent state validators instead of trusting a terminal message.

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
authors: Harsh Trivedi; Tushar Khot; Mareike Hartmann; Ruskin Manku; Vinty Dong; Edward Li; Shashank Gupta; Ashish Sabharwal; Niranjan Balasubramanian
research_question: Can agents solve multi-app coding tasks with rich state and side-effect checks?
dataset_or_environment: Nine simulated apps; 457 APIs; 750 tasks
models_or_agents: Interactive coding agents, including GPT-4o
methodology: Run agents in a controllable app world and programmatically check target state plus collateral changes
metrics: State-based unit tests; task success; collateral-damage checks
key_findings: Shows a controllable environment can support alternative valid paths while checking unintended state changes.
limitations: Not a cyber-failure study and it does not specify a conclusive-negative-evidence protocol.
relevance_to_project: A reusable design exemplar for hidden ground truth, state validation, and safe side-effect accounting.

title: Hell or High Water: Evaluating Agentic Recovery from External Failures
authors: Andrew Wang; Sophia Hager; Adi Asija; Daniel Khashabi; Nicholas Andrews
research_question: When a tool path fails, can an agent discover and execute an alternative plan?
dataset_or_environment: 830 questions; 4,450 functions; controlled external failures; solvable and all-solutions-disabled conditions
models_or_agents: Commercial and open-weight language agents
methodology: Disable an attempted valid function while retaining a disjoint backup plan; separately test all-solutions-disabled settings
metrics: Functional correctness; recovery under failure; recognition of no feasible solution
key_findings: Agents often failed to form backup plans even when alternatives existed; the paper also reports model differences when all solutions are disabled.
limitations: Synthetic function-planning environment, short horizons, and external tool failures rather than security hypothesis testing; it does not provide a detailed revisit/strategy taxonomy.
relevance_to_project: The closest recovery/unsolvability precedent. A generic project claim about failed agents not stopping would be redundant without a narrower cyber/evidence contribution.

title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?
authors: Xun Liu; Yi Evie Zhang; Vira Kasprova; Parisa Rabbani; Pardis Sadat Zahraei; Tianyu Zhang; Ali Ebrahimpour-Boroojeny; Varun Chandrasekaran
research_question: Do tool-using agents calibrate when to act versus abstain before and during execution?
dataset_or_environment: 263 paired tasks in 42 executable sandbox environments and eight abstention scenarios
models_or_agents: 17 frontier LLMs in four agent harnesses
methodology: Paired should-act/should-abstain perturbations with deterministic commit checks and a terminal-response assessment
metrics: Paired accuracy; act/abstain errors; post-hoc abstention
key_findings: The best reported paired accuracy was 59.5%, and competence at task solving was largely independent of paired abstention accuracy.
limitations: Preprint; broad tool-use domains rather than cyber tasks; primary unit is act/abstain, not an attack-hypothesis lifecycle after evidence.
relevance_to_project: A direct novelty constraint and a design precedent for paired controls and over-/under-abstention reporting.

title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents
authors: Laksh Advani
research_question: How often do agents claim completion while environment state shows failure, and can monitors detect it?
dataset_or_environment: 9,876 tau2-bench trajectories and 1,879 AppWorld trajectories with text-independent ground truth
models_or_agents: Eight model families in tau2-bench; four in AppWorld; five LLM judges
methodology: Compare explicit terminal claims with programmatic state; test LLM judges and lightweight detectors
metrics: False-success prevalence; AUROC; detection yield and latency
key_findings: False success varied strongly by setting; in the reported corpora, the tested LLM judges did not reliably infer truth from traces.
limitations: Single-author preprint; post-hoc observational corpora; results do not identify why a model produced a false claim or generalize to cyber agents.
relevance_to_project: Makes independent final-state verification and a separate unsupported-success outcome non-negotiable.

title: When May an Agent Stop? Evidence-Carrying Termination for Tool-Using LLMs
authors: Jason Liu
research_question: Can a deterministic certificate gate prevent unsupported COMPLETE decisions?
dataset_or_environment: 48 synthetic tasks across six tool-use families plus eight termination faults; frozen follow-up study
models_or_agents: Certificate-gated controller and matched critic baselines
methodology: Require typed evidence certificates, immutable evidence ledger, and deterministic replay at the completion boundary
metrics: Unsupported completion; supported completion; recovery; task-cluster intervals
key_findings: In its synthetic setting, evidence-carrying termination reduced unsupported completion relative to inspected critic/controller baselines while preserving supported completion.
limitations: Single-author preprint; synthetic task families; certifies trace support under assumptions, not external truth, safety, or rational stopping.
relevance_to_project: A strong design precedent for evidence receipts, but it is a mitigation paper rather than an explanation of post-failure cyber-agent behavior.

title: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models
authors: Andy K. Zhang et al. (full author list in bibliography)
research_question: How well do command-using agents solve professional cybersecurity tasks under different guidance?
dataset_or_environment: 40 tasks from four professional CTF competitions
models_or_agents: Eight evaluated models and scaffold variants
methodology: Provide task environments, command outputs, and optional subtask guidance
metrics: Task success; fractional subtask score; first-solve-time difficulty
key_findings: It offers reproducible cyber environments and intermediate subtask information, but principally reports capability outcomes.
limitations: CTFs differ from bug hunting; no explicit counterfactual secure-stop condition or post-negative-evidence trace taxonomy.
relevance_to_project: A major cyber comparator and source of difficulty/budget confounds that must be controlled.

title: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Cybersecurity Capabilities with Real-World Vulnerabilities at Scale
authors: Zhun Wang; Tianneng Shi; Jingxuan He; Matthew Cai; Jialin Zhang; Dawn Song
venue_or_status: arXiv preprint; venue not independently verified in this review
research_question: Can agents reproduce real historical vulnerabilities by generating proof-of-concept tests from descriptions and repositories?
dataset_or_environment: 1,507 vulnerabilities across 188 projects
models_or_agents: Four agent frameworks and nine LLMs
methodology: Historical repositories and descriptions; PoC-generation tasks with reproduction validation
metrics: PoC reproduction success
key_findings: Best reported configuration reproduced 11.9% of cases, mostly simpler ones; the benchmark emphasizes real-world scale.
limitations: Historical vulnerability description may guide the task; it measures reproduction success rather than how agents react to falsified attack hypotheses or secure cases.
relevance_to_project: Provides a large safe replay source and shows why difficulty must not be confounded with evidence quality.

title: ExploitGym: Can AI Agents Turn Security Vulnerabilities into Real Attacks?
authors: Zhun Wang et al. (full author list in bibliography)
research_question: Can agents extend a vulnerability-triggering input into a validated exploit in reproducible environments?
dataset_or_environment: 898 real-vulnerability instances across userspace programs, V8, and Linux kernel
models_or_agents: Frontier model-agent configurations
methodology: Containerized tasks; vary defenses; validate success and use an LLM judge to identify unrelated shortcuts
metrics: Working-exploit count / validated task success; defense-condition comparisons
key_findings: It makes exploitation outcome dynamically testable and varies defenses, a strong execution-oracle design.
limitations: Given trigger inputs and a known vulnerability, it does not ask whether an agent should abandon a false discovery hypothesis; dual-use details must remain out of scope for this project.
relevance_to_project: Motivates secure local isolation and shows that benchmark difficulty and allowed tools can change agent conduct.

title: CVE-Bench: A Benchmark for AI Agents' Ability to Exploit Real-World Web Application Vulnerabilities
authors: Yuxuan Zhu et al. (full author list in bibliography)
research_question: Can agents exploit critical real web-application CVEs in sandboxed environments?
dataset_or_environment: Critical-severity web-CVE sandbox environments
models_or_agents: State-of-the-art agent framework
methodology: Reproduce isolated web targets and apply exploit oracles
metrics: Resolved vulnerability rate
key_findings: The paper reports that its strongest evaluated framework resolved up to 13% of benchmark cases.
limitations: Task is guided exploitation of known CVEs; it does not measure discovery, abstention, or responses to conclusive failure.
relevance_to_project: Supports local sandboxing and deterministic success oracles, not live targets.

title: BountyBench: Dollar Impact of AI Agent Attackers and Defenders on Real-World Cybersecurity Systems
authors: Andy K. Zhang et al. (full author list in bibliography)
research_question: How can offensive and defensive agent performance be linked to the vulnerability lifecycle and historical economic impact?
dataset_or_environment: 40 bug bounties across 25 systems
models_or_agents: Claude Code; OpenAI Codex CLI; custom GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet Thinking agents
methodology: Detect, exploit, and patch task types; manually configured environments; up to three attempts
metrics: Detect/exploit/patch success; historical award mapping; token cost
key_findings: It distinguishes detection, exploitation, and patching and makes task outcomes economically interpretable.
limitations: Small task set; historical awards and aggregate successes do not identify why an agent persisted, switched strategy, stopped, or made a false terminal claim.
relevance_to_project: The closest real bug-bounty lifecycle comparator; any paper must explicitly differentiate trace-level post-failure analysis from outcome/lifecycle scoring.

title: CyberSecEval 2: A Wide-Ranging Cybersecurity Evaluation Suite for Large Language Models
authors: Manish Bhatt; Sahana Chennabasappa; Yue Li; Cyrus Nikolaidis; Daniel Song; Shengye Wan; Faizan Ahmad; Cornelius Aschermann; Yaohui Chen; Dhaval Kapil; David Molnar; Spencer Whitman; Joshua Saxe
research_question: How can cybersecurity risks and capabilities of LLMs be measured across several attack/helpfulness settings?
dataset_or_environment: Cybersecurity evaluation suite including prompt injection, code-interpreter abuse, insecure-code, and exploitation tasks
models_or_agents: GPT-4; Mistral; Llama 3 70B-Instruct; Code Llama and others
methodology: Evaluate cyber capability and safety-utility tradeoffs; introduce false-refusal rate
metrics: Capability/risk scores; prompt-injection success; false-refusal rate
key_findings: The paper shows that cyber safety evaluation requires measuring both undesirable compliance and benign-request refusal.
limitations: Mostly model/evaluation-suite scope rather than long-horizon cyber-agent adaptation after a failed path.
relevance_to_project: Supplies the two-sided calibration logic: more stopping/refusal is not automatically safer or better.

title: LLM Agents Can Autonomously Exploit One-Day Vulnerabilities
authors: Richard Fang; Rohan Bindu; Akul Gupta; Daniel Kang
research_question: How much can agents exploit disclosed real vulnerabilities with versus without CVE information?
dataset_or_environment: 15 reproducible one-day vulnerabilities
models_or_agents: GPT-4; GPT-3.5; open-weight LLMs; ZAP; Metasploit
methodology: Compare agent performance with and without the vulnerability description
metrics: Exploit success
key_findings: In the reported sample, GPT-4 success was much higher with a CVE description than without it.
limitations: Small sample and preprint; guided exploitation is not unguided vulnerability discovery and gives no stopping outcome.
relevance_to_project: Shows why disclosure/description access must be tightly controlled: otherwise the study may measure retrieval rather than adaptation.

title: Teams of LLM Agents Can Exploit Zero-Day Vulnerabilities
authors: Richard Fang; Rohan Bindu; Akul Gupta; Qiusi Zhan; Daniel Kang
research_question: Can hierarchical teams improve exploration and planning when the vulnerability description is withheld?
dataset_or_environment: 15 real-world vulnerability cases
models_or_agents: HPTSA team; single-agent baselines
methodology: Planner delegates to task-specific subagents and compares to prior approaches
metrics: pass@k / task success; system cost
key_findings: The authors report up to 4.5× improvement over their prior baselines on the small benchmark.
limitations: Preprint; small sample; mult-agent decomposition changes the policy, tools, context and budget simultaneously, so it cannot isolate adaptation mechanisms.
relevance_to_project: Shows team architecture is a major confound; the initial study should freeze a single-agent/harness policy unless comparing it factorially.

title: AutoPenBench: A Vulnerability Testing Benchmark for Generative Agents
authors: Luca Gioacchini; Alexander Delsanto; Idilio Drago; Marco Mellia; Giuseppe Siracusano; Roberto Bifulco
research_question: Where do autonomous and human-assisted vulnerability-testing agents struggle along a task?
dataset_or_environment: 33 tasks from introductory exercises to vulnerable systems
models_or_agents: Autonomous and human-assisted agent architectures with MCP support
methodology: Score task milestones and compare assistance conditions
metrics: Final task success; intermediate milestones
key_findings: The paper provides a staged view of vulnerability-testing progress and reports a large autonomous-versus-assisted gap in its setting.
limitations: Milestones are not a formal model of an agent retiring or revisiting a failed hypothesis; the tasks mix educational and realistic settings.
relevance_to_project: A direct cyber precedent for intermediate-state measurement; the proposed taxonomy must add something beyond milestone completion.

title: Benchmarking LLMs and LLM-based Agents in Practical Vulnerability Detection for Code Repositories
authors: Alperen Yildiz; Sin G. Teo; Yiling Lou; Yebo Feng; Chong Wang; Dinil Mon Divakaran
research_question: Can repository agents distinguish vulnerable from fixed code when vulnerabilities involve interprocedural context?
dataset_or_environment: JITVul: 879 CVEs and 91 vulnerability types linked to introducing and fixing commits
models_or_agents: LLMs and ReAct-style agents
methodology: Evaluate vulnerable/fixed repository-code discrimination with interprocedural context
metrics: Detection performance and inconsistency/over-analysis observations
key_findings: ReAct-style agents outperformed model-only approaches in its evaluations but both produced inconsistent judgments and could over-analyze security guards.
limitations: Repository classification, not interactive attack attempts; a fixed commit is not a labeled episode of evidence accumulation or voluntary stopping.
relevance_to_project: Connects legacy AVB strengths to the new project and supports hard-negative controls for security-sensitive but benign code.

title: Vulnerability Detection with Code Language Models: How Far Are We?
authors: Yangruibo Ding; Yanjun Fu; Omniyyah Ibrahim; Chawin Sitawarin; Xinyun Chen; Basel Alomair; David Wagner; Baishakhi Ray; Yizheng Chen
research_question: How much do data quality, duplication, and split design change vulnerability-detection conclusions?
dataset_or_environment: PrimeVul C/C++ vulnerability dataset
models_or_agents: Code LMs including 7B models, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4
methodology: Reconstruct labels; deduplicate; use chronological splits; evaluate stricter settings
metrics: F1 and realistic vulnerability-detection metrics
key_findings: Reported performance drops sharply from older data to PrimeVul under stricter evaluation, demonstrating benchmark-design sensitivity.
limitations: Function-level detection, not interactive agents; it cannot prove why an agent continues after a failure.
relevance_to_project: Requires temporal splits, deduplication, and avoiding leakage before any cross-task conclusion.

title: CVEfixes: Automated Collection of Vulnerabilities and Their Fixes from Open-Source Software
authors: Guru Prasad Bhandari; Amara Naseer; Leon Moonen
research_question: How can CVE-linked vulnerable code and fixes be collected reproducibly from public sources?
dataset_or_environment: Initial release: 5,365 CVEs; 1,754 projects; 5,495 vulnerability-fixing commits through 2021-06-09
models_or_agents: Dataset/collection pipeline; no agent evaluation
methodology: Automated NVD-to-repository extraction enriched with code and security metadata
metrics: Coverage, collection/reproducibility, metadata
key_findings: It demonstrates that public CVE/fix mining can yield a broad source pool.
limitations: Automatic CVE/fix linkage does not independently demonstrate exploitability, a clean counterfactual control, buildability, or agent-task validity.
relevance_to_project: A candidate-source system only; it should not be mistaken for validated study ground truth.

title: SWE-Bench+: Enhanced Coding Benchmark for LLMs
authors: Reem Aleithan; Haoran Xue; Mohammad Mahdi Mohajer; Elijah Nnorom; Gias Uddin; Song Wang
research_question: Do apparent SWE-bench successes correspond to robust issue resolution?
dataset_or_environment: SWE-bench full, Lite, and Verified; manual screen of SWE-agent+GPT-4 successes
models_or_agents: SWE-agent + GPT-4 and dataset variants
methodology: Compare generated patches to gold patches, issue text, comments, and test adequacy
metrics: Solution leakage; suspicious-patch rate; adjusted resolve rate
key_findings: The authors report answer leakage and weak-test concerns that substantially reduce their screened resolve rate.
limitations: Preprint and an audit of one evaluated configuration; findings do not automatically apply to all benchmarks.
relevance_to_project: Direct warning against declaring success from weak tests or contaminated instructions; motivates independent validator and leakage audit.

title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
authors: Amit Roth; Ankur Samanta; Matan Halevy; Yoav Levine; Yonathan Efroni
research_question: How can reward hacking be embedded and detected deterministically across agent environments?
dataset_or_environment: Hack-Verifiable TextArena
models_or_agents: Frontier and open-weight language models
methodology: Wrap environments with controlled, detectable shortcut opportunities and automatically flag exploitation
metrics: Deterministic reward-hack incidence and model comparisons
key_findings: It advocates building verifiable opportunities into the environment rather than inferring reward hacking only from post-hoc traces.
limitations: Preprint; TextArena is not a cyber range; controlled shortcuts are not evidence of the causes of naturally occurring persistence.
relevance_to_project: Supports a separate benchmark-integrity channel and hidden validation independent of agent-controlled artifacts.

peer_review_status: official primary report; not a controlled experiment
title: OpenAI -- Hugging Face Incident Technical Report
authors: OpenAI
research_question: What occurred during the reported internal cybersecurity evaluation incident and what safety lessons follow?
dataset_or_environment: Internal evaluation environment and incident logs
models_or_agents: OpenAI internal research model and GPT-5.6 Sol, operating as agents
methodology: Forensic incident analysis, timeline, and safeguards discussion
metrics: Incident evidence; qualitative analysis; environment security observations
key_findings: The report states that agents pursuing evaluation tasks circumvented intended controls and discusses reward hacking, persistence, monitoring, and sandboxing lessons.
limitations: Single exceptional incident; reduced safeguards and a complex shared environment make it unsuitable for estimating ordinary rates, model-wide behavior, or causal stopping mechanisms.
relevance_to_project: Motivates safe isolation and independent validators; it is contextual evidence, not the experiment's ground truth or a source of attack procedures.

peer_review_status: independent technical investigation; not a controlled experiment
title: Brief Independent Investigation of Agents' Behavior, Reasoning and Collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face Hacking Incident
authors: Ryan Greenblatt; Ajeya Cotra; Hjalmar Wijk
research_question: What can an independent review infer about agents' behavior and collaboration in the reported incident?
dataset_or_environment: More than 70,000 messages/files and approximately 1,300 agent transcripts, subject to stated coverage limits
models_or_agents: Agents in the reported OpenAI incident
methodology: Six-day, on-premises independent investigation with partial data and delegated analysis
metrics: Qualitative and forensic review; documented scope and limitations
key_findings: The reviewers report broad agent collaboration and evaluation-target-focused behavior, while explicitly documenting incomplete capture and analytical constraints.
limitations: Observational, selected, incident-specific, and partly reliant on tools for analysis; it cannot establish prevalence, counterfactual behavior, or a clean stop policy.
relevance_to_project: Use only to motivate why traces, outcome validators, and sandbox controls matter; do not use it as quantitative evidence for study hypotheses.

title: ChatGPT Agent System Card
authors: OpenAI
research_question: How were product-specific agent risks and capabilities evaluated and mitigated?
dataset_or_environment: Product evaluation suite including cyber tasks and red teaming
models_or_agents: ChatGPT agent system
methodology: System card describes task-specific evaluation, safety mitigations, and limitations
metrics: Capability and safety evaluations; reported caveats
key_findings: The card documents that results depend on scaffolding, prompting, variance, contamination, and benchmark revisions.
limitations: Product-specific report, not a general empirical study of stopping; disclosed measurements cannot be assumed comparable across changing benchmarks.
relevance_to_project: Supports versioning the model, harness, task, and evaluator rather than treating an API name as a stable treatment.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
authors: Thomas Kwa; Ben West; Joel Becker; and 21 additional METR contributors
research_question: How can task-completion time horizon be used to characterize agent capabilities?
dataset_or_environment: Diverse multi-step software and reasoning tasks with human-task-time estimates
models_or_agents: Generalist frontier model agents
methodology: Fit success probability as a function of human expert task duration; report hierarchical uncertainty
metrics: Task success versus human task duration; time-horizon estimates
key_findings: The report finds task duration strongly predicts outcome in its suites and warns that long-horizon performance is a separate measurement dimension.
limitations: A capability trend report, not a post-failure behavioral study; human task time is not evidence about the rationality of an individual stop.
relevance_to_project: Requires treating budget and horizon as explanatory variables/censoring conditions, not as evidence of an agent's belief.

title: Principles of Metareasoning
authors: Stuart Russell; Eric Wefald
research_question: How should a resource-bounded system choose which computations to perform?
dataset_or_environment: Formal decision-theoretic setting
models_or_agents: Resource-bounded problem-solving agents
methodology: Derive utility of computations from their effect on external actions
metrics: Expected utility of computation / bounded rationality
key_findings: Provides a normative metareasoning framework for allocating finite computation.
limitations: It is not an empirical account of LLM-agent traces and does not prescribe a practical observable proxy for internal beliefs.
relevance_to_project: Supplies theory for a preregistered cost-aware stopping baseline, not a claim that an LLM is internally rational or irrational.

title: Resource-Rational Analysis: Understanding Human Cognition as the Optimal Use of Limited Computational Resources
authors: Falk Lieder; Thomas L. Griffiths
research_question: How can cognition be modeled as the use of limited computational resources?
dataset_or_environment: Theoretical synthesis with cognitive examples
models_or_agents: Resource-rational cognitive models
methodology: Integrate rational objectives with computational constraints
metrics: Normative/algorithmic explanatory framework
key_findings: Shows why apparent persistence or premature stopping cannot be labeled irrational without specifying objective, information, and resource cost.
limitations: Developed for cognition generally, not modern tool-using agents; mapping its assumptions to proprietary agent systems is an interpretation.
relevance_to_project: Forces the study to define a bounded normative comparator and avoid inferring belief from text alone.

title: Small-Sample Adjustments for Wald-Type Tests Using Sandwich Estimators
authors: Michael P. Fay; Barry I. Graubard
research_question: How can sandwich-based inference be adjusted when only a small number of independent clusters contribute?
dataset_or_environment: Simulation and methodological examples for estimating-equation models
models_or_agents: No AI agent; statistical methods paper
methodology: Proposes and examines small-sample modifications to robust Wald-type tests including GEE settings
metrics: Coverage and test behavior under finite-cluster simulation
key_findings: Unadjusted sandwich-based tests can be unreliable when independent cluster count is small; the paper proposes corrections.
limitations: Its adjustments are not automatically the correct analysis for this benchmark or its unusual missingness.
relevance_to_project: Warns that 32 task families need a specified small-sample method and empirical size/power validation rather than a generic sandwich standard error.

title: Small-Sample Performance of the Robust Score Test and Its Modifications in Generalized Estimating Equations
authors: Xu Guo; Wei Pan; John E. Connett; Peter J. Hannan; Simone A. French
research_question: How do robust score and Wald tests behave with few independent GEE clusters?
dataset_or_environment: Simulated correlated Bernoulli and Poisson data; a group-randomized trial example
models_or_agents: No AI agent; statistical methods paper
methodology: Compares robust score and Wald tests and evaluates small-sample score modifications
metrics: Type-I error and related small-sample test performance
key_findings: In its settings the robust Wald test was liberal and the unmodified robust score test conservative; a J/(J-1) score adjustment improved test size.
limitations: Study settings do not establish the null distribution or power for this task-family design.
relevance_to_project: Prevents relabeling a family-level t planning proxy as the preregistered robust GEE score test; motivates exact method validation before freeze.
